groups.description: Crop and livestock statistics, physical commodity prices, and trade flows. The interesting property of this group is the estimate-then-settle pattern: a production forecast is issued monthly, revised monthly, and eventually replaced by a survey. That is a correction-latency dimension with a real anchor at the end of it, which few other domains offer.

entries.name: USDA NASS Quick Stats
entries.why: Census and survey estimates for every US crop, with survey results superseding forecasts.

entries.name: USDA Economic Research Service Data
entries.why: Farm income and food price outlook series, revised on a published calendar.

entries.name: USDA FAS Production, Supply and Distribution
entries.why: Global balance sheets by commodity, which FAO and traders both republish downstream.

entries.name: USDA FAS Export Sales Reporting
entries.why: Weekly export sales on a fixed Thursday release, so a late file is visible immediately.

entries.name: USDA AMS Market News
entries.why: Physical cash prices for produce, meat, and grain, reported several times a day.

entries.name: USDA WASDE
entries.why: The monthly estimate that moves grain markets, with every prior month restated beside it.

entries.name: USDA Cropland Data Layer
entries.why: Annual land cover raster, reissued with method changes that a schema-stability test catches.

entries.name: FAO FAOSTAT
entries.why: The global reference series, largely derivative of national statistics offices.

entries.name: FAO AQUASTAT
entries.why: Water use by country and sector, sparse enough to exercise completeness by segment.

entries.name: FAO FishStat
entries.why: Capture and aquaculture production, a domain no other registry entry covers.

entries.name: AMIS Market Database
entries.why: A G20 aggregation of USDA, FAO, and national numbers, so lineage is the whole product.

entries.name: FEWS NET
entries.why: Food security classifications on a scheduled outlook, with revisions between releases.

entries.name: UN Comtrade
entries.why: Bilateral trade flows where each pair is reported twice and rarely agrees, which is a built-in internal consistency test.

entries.name: WTO Timeseries
entries.why: Tariff and trade indicators, derivative of member notifications with long lags.

entries.name: ITC Trade Map
entries.why: A Comtrade derivative with its own estimates filled in, which makes the lineage visible.

entries.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries
entries.why: Annual production and reserves per mineral, with estimates flagged as such in the source.

entries.name: OPEC Reference Basket Price
entries.why: One daily number with a named formula, which is the simplest possible reproducibility test.

entries.name: CME Group Daily Settlements
entries.why: Public settlement files anchor the cash prices elsewhere in this group. Terms need a careful read before anything is routed, because exchange data is licensed aggressively.

entries.name: ICE Public Reports
entries.why: A second exchange publishing settlements, which gives CME a cross-venue comparison.

entries.name: LME Official Prices
entries.reason: LME price data is sold under a market data licence with per-user reporting obligations. Redistribution through a router is exactly what that licence prices, so this is a customer-credentials case at best, and not before Phase 2.
entries.why: The metals benchmark. Named here so nobody researches the licence a second time.

groups.description: Sanctions lists, procurement, lobbying, campaign finance, and political event data. Sanctions lists are the one group in the registry where staleness is a compliance failure rather than an inconvenience, which makes freshness lag the dimension that matters most and the one a caller would actually pay to have measured. Most of the rest is derivative of filings that are already elsewhere in the registry, which makes the group a good lineage exhibit.

entries.name: OFAC Sanctions Lists
entries.why: The list where an hour of staleness is a compliance problem, which is the strongest argument for a freshness-lag number that anyone outside this project will recognise.

entries.name: EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List
entries.why: The same designations as OFAC with different timing, so disagreement is real and dateable.

entries.name: UK OFSI Consolidated List
entries.why: A third list covering overlapping entities, which makes a three-way compare meaningful.

entries.name: UN Security Council Consolidated List
entries.why: The upstream that national lists implement, so the lag between them is the lineage.

entries.name: World Bank Debarred Firms
entries.why: Exclusions with start and end dates, so an expired entry that lingers is a visible error.

entries.name: Open Ownership Register
entries.why: Beneficial ownership in a standard schema, collected from registers of uneven quality.

entries.name: Tenders Electronic Daily
entries.why: EU tender notices published daily with corrigenda, which is correction latency in public.

entries.name: Contracts Finder
entries.why: UK notices in OCDS, the same schema as TED, so a cross-country compare is cheap.

entries.name: SAM.gov Entity and Exclusions
entries.why: US federal exclusions and entity registrations, joinable to usaspending already in the registry.

entries.name: Senate Lobbying Disclosure
entries.why: Quarterly filings with amendments that supersede, which is our snapshot model exactly.

entries.name: OpenSecrets
entries.why: A derivative of FEC and Senate LDA filings, both of which we already plan to carry.

entries.name: FollowTheMoney
entries.why: State-level campaign finance, the one layer federal sources do not reach.

entries.name: EU Transparency Register
entries.why: Self-declared lobbying data, where internal consistency checks find real contradictions.

entries.name: Open States
entries.why: Fifty state legislatures normalised, with per-state scrapers that fail independently.

entries.name: LegiScan
entries.why: A second read on the same state bills, which makes Open States checkable against a peer.

entries.name: GDELT Project
entries.why: A fifteen-minute event feed built from news text, and therefore the largest untrusted_text surface we would carry. Skeptic review before anything is promoted.

entries.name: ACLED
entries.why: Coded conflict events that are revised retroactively as reports are reconciled.

entries.name: Transparency International CPI
entries.why: A composite of other surveys, published annually, with the source list stated. Lineage.

entries.name: Varieties of Democracy
entries.why: Expert-coded indices with confidence intervals, which no other registry entry carries.

entries.name: Our World in Data
entries.why: Openly derivative of almost everything else here, with the upstream named per chart, which makes it the single best lineage inference test in the registry.

groups.description: Cultural heritage collections, media metadata, and sports results. The heritage half is slow, open, and heavily attributed, which exercises the attribution string in license_chain more than any other group. The sports half is the opposite: seconds matter, corrections are common during a game, and the settled result at the end is a genuine anchor. Phase 4 names graded sports feeds as a vertical, so these entries are targets rather than hypotheses.

entries.name: The Movie Database
entries.why: Community-edited film metadata with a daily export, so edits are diffable in bulk.

entries.name: Discogs
entries.why: Release metadata that overlaps MusicBrainz, so two community catalogs can be compared.

entries.name: ListenBrainz
entries.why: Listening statistics under CC0, joined to MusicBrainz identifiers we already plan to carry.

entries.name: Spotify Web API
entries.why: Catalog metadata behind per-user OAuth, which only works as pass-through. Terms almost certainly forbid the caching a router does, so read them before promising anything.

entries.name: Europeana
entries.why: An aggregator over thousands of institutions with per-item rights statements, which is a licence chain with a different licence on every row.

entries.name: Digital Public Library of America
entries.why: The US counterpart to Europeana, with the same per-item rights problem.

entries.name: Smithsonian Open Access
entries.why: CC0 collection records with stable identifiers, the simplest licence case in the group.

entries.name: Metropolitan Museum of Art Collection API
entries.why: No key, no quota, small payloads, which makes it a good first end-to-end console demo.

entries.name: Rijksmuseum API
entries.why: A national collection with strict attribution wording that must be reproduced verbatim.

entries.name: Harvard Art Museums API
entries.why: Records carry a lastupdate field, so freshness can be measured without guessing.

entries.name: Chronicling America
entries.why: OCR text of historical newspapers, which is bulk untrusted_text with no live risk.

entries.name: Library of Congress JSON API
entries.why: One API over many collections whose schemas differ, a real schema-stability workout.

entries.name: HathiTrust Bibliographic API
entries.why: Holdings and rights per volume, where the rights field is the point rather than a footnote.

entries.name: Directory of Open Access Journals
entries.why: Journal licensing metadata, which is the reference table a licence chain needs anyway.

entries.name: Project Gutenberg
entries.why: A catalog that is public domain in content but trademark-restricted in distribution, which is a licence nuance the schema should be able to express.

entries.name: Wikimedia Pageviews and REST API
entries.why: Hourly counts that are restated after bot filtering, a clean revision-behaviour example.

entries.name: New York Times Developer APIs
entries.why: Archive and books metadata under terms that will almost certainly block commercial use, which makes it a concrete test of the two-endpoint split in ADR-0008.

entries.name: MLB Stats API
entries.why: Live play-by-play that is corrected during and after a game, then settled officially. That settled result is a real anchor, which accuracy claims need under rule H1.

entries.name: NHL Web API
entries.why: A second league on the same pattern, unofficial docs only, so stability is the question.

entries.name: football-data.org
entries.why: A derivative results feed with a free tier, so its lag behind the league is measurable.

groups.description: Electricity markets, grid operators, and emissions accounting. Grid operators publish on a five-minute clock and then revise settlement data for weeks, which makes this the group with the sharpest revision behaviour and correction latency signals in the registry. Emissions inventories sit at the other end: annual, heavily restated, and mostly derivative.

entries.name: ENTSO-E Transparency Platform
entries.why: Generation, load, and prices for every EU bidding zone, revised after settlement.

entries.name: Elexon BMRS
entries.why: GB balancing mechanism at half-hourly settlement, with initial and final runs to diff.

entries.name: NESO Data Portal
entries.why: GB system operator forecasts, which lets forecast against outturn be measured directly.

entries.name: CAISO OASIS
entries.why: California nodal prices, with a published schedule of when each report becomes final.

entries.name: ERCOT Market Information System
entries.why: Texas load and price files on a fixed posting cadence, so lateness is unambiguous.

entries.name: PJM Data Miner 2
entries.why: The largest US market, and it restates settlement prices openly after the fact.

entries.name: MISO Market Reports
entries.why: A second US RTO publishing the same quantities, which gives a cross-operator anchor.

entries.name: NYISO Market and Operational Data
entries.why: Flat CSV files on a strict clock, cheap to snapshot and easy to diff.

entries.name: AEMO NEMWEB
entries.why: Australian dispatch every five minutes, in a timezone that stresses our clock handling.

entries.name: Energy-Charts (Fraunhofer ISE)
entries.why: A derivative of ENTSO-E and national operators, so it is a ready-made lineage test.

entries.name: Electricity Maps
entries.why: Carbon intensity per zone, derived from grid operators, with a free noncommercial tier.

entries.name: UK Carbon Intensity API
entries.why: Forecast and actual in the same endpoint, which is the cleanest accuracy anchor we have.

entries.name: IEA Statistics
entries.reason: The headline statistics are sold under a paid licence that restricts redistribution. Trooth does not buy data it then resells (section 2), so this can only arrive as a pass-through under a customer's own subscription, and not before Phase 2.
entries.why: The reference series everyone benchmarks against, which is exactly why it is not free.

entries.name: IRENA Renewable Capacity Statistics
entries.why: Annual capacity by country, restated often enough to be a revision-behaviour example.

entries.name: NOAA GHCN-Daily
entries.why: Station observations quality-controlled after publication, so past values change.

entries.name: Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service
entries.why: Forecast and reanalysis of the same field, which separates freshness from accuracy.

entries.name: Global Carbon Budget
entries.why: An annual release that revises every prior year, which is a revision story in one file.

entries.name: Climate TRACE
entries.why: Facility-level emissions estimates, useful only if the method version travels with them.

entries.name: EDGAR Emissions Database (JRC)
entries.notes: Unrelated to SEC EDGAR, which is already in the registry as sec-edgar.
entries.why: The European inventory that other emissions estimates are routinely compared against.

entries.name: NREL Developer Network
entries.why: Solar resource, utility rates, and fuel stations behind one api.data.gov key.

groups.description: Disasters, hazards, and environmental monitoring. An alert feed is the one place where every dimension we measure has an obvious cost attached: late is dangerous, wrong is worse, and a silent revision after the fact is how people stop trusting a source. Several entries here duplicate each other deliberately, because two agencies reporting the same earthquake with different magnitudes is the clearest possible demonstration of what compare is for.

entries.name: Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System
entries.why: A multi-hazard alert layer over other agencies, which makes it derivative by design.

entries.name: EM-DAT International Disaster Database
entries.why: Disaster losses restated for years after the event, which is correction latency at the scale of decades rather than minutes.

entries.name: ReliefWeb
entries.why: Situation reports as documents, so the payload is untrusted_text almost end to end.

entries.name: USGS Volcano Hazards Program
entries.why: Alert level changes with an explicit issue time, which is a state machine with timestamps.

entries.name: Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program
entries.why: The global catalog USGS reports flow into weekly, a lineage pair with a known lag.

entries.name: NASA FIRMS Active Fire Data
entries.why: Near-real-time detections replaced by standard-quality ones days later, so the same fire appears twice with different values. A revision-behaviour example that needs no explanation.

entries.name: European Forest Fire Information System
entries.why: A regional derivative of FIRMS, which lets a lineage claim be checked against a peer.

entries.name: InciWeb
entries.why: Incident narratives updated irregularly by hand, so freshness varies wildly by incident.

entries.name: NIFC Open Data
entries.why: Perimeters and situation reports with edit timestamps, the structured half of InciWeb.

entries.name: NOAA National Hurricane Center
entries.why: Advisories every three hours on a fixed clock, with forecast tracks that can be scored against the track that actually happened. A rare anchored accuracy case.

entries.name: IBTrACS Tropical Cyclone Best Track
entries.why: The settled reanalysis of storms, which is the anchor NHC forecasts are scored against.

entries.name: US Drought Monitor
entries.why: A weekly expert judgement over several inputs, so the method is human and documented.

entries.name: NSIDC Sea Ice Index
entries.why: Daily near-real-time values later replaced by a final product, clearly labelled as such.

entries.name: Copernicus Emergency Management Service
entries.why: Activation-based mapping, so coverage is zero until an event, which segments completeness.

entries.name: European Environment Agency Air Quality
entries.why: Up-to-date and validated streams of the same stations, published as separate products.

entries.name: EPA Air Quality System
entries.why: The certified archive behind AirNow, which is already in the registry as the fast feed. Together they are a freshness and accuracy trade-off with both ends in our hands.

entries.name: EPA Toxics Release Inventory
entries.why: Self-reported annual releases with preliminary and updated versions of the same year.

entries.name: NOAA Tsunami Warning Centers
entries.why: Messages issued and then cancelled, where the cancellation matters as much as the alert.

entries.name: EMSC Seismic Portal
entries.why: Reports the same earthquakes as usgs-earthquake, our first merged source, with a different magnitude and a different lag. That disagreement is the demo the compare tool exists for, against a source whose catalog entry is already written.

entries.name: GFZ GEOFON
entries.why: A third seismic network, which turns a two-way disagreement into a majority question.

groups.description: Central banks, international statistical agencies, market data, and crypto. Financial data is where redistribution terms bite hardest: several widely used endpoints are free to call and still forbid republication, which is exactly the distinction the licence chain exists to carry. Nothing here is promoted without reading the terms in full.

entries.name: ECB euro foreign exchange reference rates
entries.why: Published once daily at a fixed time, so it is a cheap and exact accuracy anchor for FX.

entries.name: Frankfurter
entries.why: Open-source republisher of ECB rates, so the lineage pair needs no licence negotiation.

entries.name: Bank of England statistics
entries.why: A second central bank, for release-schedule comparison outside the United States.

entries.name: IMF Data
entries.why: International macro series, heavily revised between vintages.

entries.name: World Bank Open Data
entries.why: Aggregates national statistics agencies, a broad lineage graph in one source.

entries.name: OECD Data Explorer
entries.why: Another derivative of national agencies, useful for republish-lag comparison.

entries.name: Eurostat
entries.why: European official statistics with a published release calendar.

entries.name: Statistics Canada
entries.why: National statistics outside the US with clear open licensing.

entries.name: UK Office for National Statistics
entries.why: Open Government Licence, a licence family we do not otherwise cover.

entries.name: Australian Bureau of Statistics
entries.why: Southern hemisphere coverage and a different release calendar shape.

entries.name: US Treasury yield curve rates
entries.why: Daily at a known time, and republished by many vendors, so lineage is easy to prove.

entries.name: CFTC Commitments of Traders
entries.why: Weekly on a fixed schedule with occasional republished corrections.

entries.name: SEC Financial Statement Data Sets
entries.why: Quarterly bulk companion to EDGAR, where restatements become visible in aggregate.

entries.name: CoinGecko
entries.why: Aggregated crypto prices, a derivative whose disagreement with exchanges is large.

entries.name: Coinbase Exchange public data
entries.why: A primary venue to compare against aggregators on the same instrument.

entries.name: Kraken public market data
entries.why: Second primary venue, so disagreement has more than two points.

entries.name: Alpha Vantage
entries.why: Free equity data tier, widely used in agent demos.

entries.name: Polygon.io
entries.why: Licensed market data, pass-through only, never redistributed by us.

entries.name: Finnhub
entries.why: Second licensed market data provider for pass-through.

entries.name: Nasdaq Data Link
entries.why: Mixed free and licensed datasets under one key, so per-dataset terms must be chained.

groups.description: Geography, mapping, aviation, marine, transit, and earth observation. This group has the tightest freshness requirements in the catalog, measured in seconds rather than hours, and it contains several sources whose terms restrict commercial use or redistribution, so the licence reading here matters more than anywhere else.

entries.name: OpenStreetMap Overpass API
entries.notes: ODbL share-alike plus a published usage policy. Needs careful reading before promotion.
entries.why: The clearest share-alike case we would route to, which forces licence chaining to work.

entries.name: Nominatim geocoding
entries.why: Geocoding, though the public instance has a strict usage policy we must respect.

entries.name: GeoNames
entries.why: Place name resolution across countries.

entries.name: Natural Earth
entries.why: Public domain basemap geometry with no attribution burden at all.

entries.name: Census TIGER/Line
entries.why: US boundary geometry, the join layer for every segment breakdown we publish.

entries.name: Aviation Weather Center METAR and TAF
entries.why: TAF forecasts graded by later METAR observations. A second anchor, same shape as NWS.

entries.name: FAA National Airspace System Status
entries.why: Ground stops and delays, where a minute of staleness changes the answer.

entries.name: FAA Aircraft Registry
entries.why: Slow-moving registry, a good schema stability baseline over years.

entries.name: OpenSky Network
entries.notes: Believed non-commercial for the free tier. Under ADR-0008 that makes it a free-endpoint source only. Confirm before promotion; this is exactly the case use classes exist for.
entries.why: Live aircraft positions, and the second non-commercial source after Open-Meteo.

entries.name: NOAA CO-OPS Tides and Currents
entries.why: Publishes predictions and verified water levels separately. A mechanical accuracy anchor.

entries.name: NOAA National Data Buoy Center
entries.why: Sensor dropouts are common and visible, which makes completeness by segment real.

entries.name: MTA GTFS-realtime
entries.why: Sub-minute freshness, which stresses the p95 lag measurement harder than anything else.

entries.name: BART GTFS-realtime
entries.why: Second transit feed, for cross-agency comparison of the same data shape.

entries.name: WMATA GTFS and realtime
entries.why: Transit coverage in a third metro area.

entries.name: Transitland
entries.why: Aggregator of agency feeds, so it is a lineage pair with each agency source.

entries.name: Bureau of Transportation Statistics
entries.why: On-time performance, published monthly on a fixed schedule.

entries.name: Copernicus Data Space
entries.why: Sentinel imagery, free and open, with a large object size worth cost modelling.

entries.name: NASA Earthdata
entries.why: Earth science across many instruments, with reprocessing as a revision event.

entries.name: NASA Open APIs
entries.why: Near-earth objects and space weather, with a free demo key for quick testing.

entries.name: NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center
entries.why: Forecasts and observations in the same feed family, so accuracy is anchorable.

groups.description: United States federal statistical, regulatory, and fiscal feeds. Most works of the US federal government are public domain under 17 U.S.C. 105, but that is a rule about authorship and not a substitute for reading a given agency's own terms, so every entry here still starts at license_status unverified. Five entries are promoted because their terms were read and cited during Phase 0.

entries.name: National Weather Service API
entries.why: Primary US weather, and the accuracy anchor where observations grade earlier forecasts.

entries.name: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program
entries.why: Magnitudes are revised after publication, which is the clearest revision behaviour we have.

entries.name: Bureau of Labor Statistics Public Data API
entries.why: Scheduled releases, so freshness lag can be measured against a published calendar.

entries.name: Federal Reserve Economic Data
entries.notes: Listed as FRED's own terms of use, not public domain. Individual series carry the terms of their originating source, which is why per-series origin notes are required.
entries.why: Republishes BLS, so republish lag is measurable and validates lineage inference.

entries.name: Open-Meteo
entries.notes: Free tier is non-commercial. Under ADR-0008 it routes only for callers who declared noncommercial, or for commercial callers who bring their own paid plan credentials.
entries.why: Derivative of NWS and others, so it demonstrates lineage lag and field disagreement.

entries.name: Bureau of Economic Analysis
entries.why: GDP advance, second, and third estimates are the cleanest revision story in public data.

entries.name: US Census American Community Survey
entries.why: Vintage-based revision and completeness that genuinely varies by geographic segment.

entries.name: US Treasury Fiscal Data
entries.why: Daily scheduled releases with exact publication times and no key required.

entries.name: Energy Information Administration
entries.why: Weekly petroleum and electricity series with routine revisions.

entries.name: SEC EDGAR
entries.notes: Requires a declared User-Agent and respects a published request rate limit.
entries.why: Restatements are revisions with legal weight, and filings carry exact acceptance times.

entries.name: Federal Register API
entries.why: Daily regulatory publication with a stable schema over a long horizon.

entries.name: Regulations.gov
entries.why: Rulemaking dockets and public comments for regulatory agents.

entries.name: USAspending
entries.why: Federal award data that is corrected heavily after first publication.

entries.name: Data.gov catalog
entries.why: A catalog of catalogs, and the fastest route to finding further candidates.

entries.name: Federal Election Commission
entries.why: Filing amendments are frequent and explicit, so revision behaviour is easy to score.

entries.name: Congress.gov API
entries.why: Bill status with defined stages, useful for correction latency.

entries.name: CPSC Recalls
entries.why: Consumer product recalls, part of the regulatory wedge alongside openFDA.

entries.name: NHTSA Recalls and Complaints
entries.why: Vehicle recalls and complaints, with duplicate reporting worth detecting.

entries.name: IRS Statistics of Income
entries.why: Slow-moving tax statistics, a good completeness-by-segment case.

entries.name: USPS ZIP Code lookup
entries.why: Address normalisation, a common preprocessing step before any geographic query.

groups.description: Routing, addressing, naming, measurement, and abuse data. Several of these are the closest public analogue to what Trooth does, in that they are measurement platforms that publish both a reading and the vantage point it was taken from. That makes them useful as prior art as well as as sources. It is also the group with the highest density of terms that forbid redistribution outright, which is worth learning early rather than late.

entries.name: RIPEstat
entries.why: Prefix, ASN, and whois views with a data_call_status field stating its own freshness.

entries.name: RIPE Atlas
entries.why: Measurements carry the probe that produced them, which is provenance done properly.

entries.name: University of Oregon Route Views
entries.why: Raw BGP archives on a fixed dump interval, so lateness is measurable to the minute.

entries.name: CAIDA BGPStream
entries.why: A derivative of Route Views and RIS, which is a lineage chain with three named hops.

entries.name: CAIDA AS Rank
entries.why: Inferred relationships, so the method version matters more than the observation date.

entries.name: PeeringDB
entries.why: Self-reported facility data, stale in exactly the way self-reported data always is.

entries.name: IPinfo
entries.why: IP geolocation where three vendors disagree constantly, which is a compare demo.

entries.name: MaxMind GeoLite2
entries.why: The second opinion IPinfo needs, on a weekly build cadence with a signed release.

entries.name: IANA RDAP Bootstrap
entries.why: The registry of registries for domain lookups, small and authoritative.

entries.name: ICANN Centralized Zone Data Service
entries.why: Zone files need a per-requester agreement per TLD, which is the pass-through model exactly.

entries.name: crt.sh Certificate Transparency
entries.why: A live append-only log with inclusion proofs, which is the Phase 2 design we plan to copy.

entries.name: Censys Search
entries.why: Host scan results with a stated scan time per record, which is freshness stated honestly.

entries.name: Shodan
entries.why: The other scanner, which makes scan staleness comparable rather than absolute.

entries.name: Cloudflare Radar
entries.why: Traffic and outage signals from one vantage point, which is the caveat worth carrying.

entries.name: OONI Measurements
entries.why: Censorship measurements with raw evidence attached, published under an open licence.

entries.name: Measurement Lab
entries.why: Public performance tests, where the pipeline restates results after post-processing.

entries.name: abuse.ch URLhaus and ThreatFox
entries.why: Indicator feeds where an entry going stale has a direct operational cost.

entries.name: Spamhaus Domain Block List
entries.reason: Free use is limited to low-volume direct queries and explicitly excludes redistribution or commercial resale. A router in front of it is the disallowed case, so this is named here only so the question is not asked again.
entries.why: The reference blocklist. Recorded as a no rather than left as an open question.

entries.name: Tranco List
entries.why: A ranking derived from four other rankings, with a permanent id per daily build.

entries.name: Majestic Million
entries.why: One of Tranco's inputs, which turns that lineage claim into something checkable.

groups.description: Population, labour, migration, and education statistics. Almost everything here is a survey, which means published confidence intervals, suppressed cells in small geographies, and scheduled restatements. That makes the group the best available test of completeness by segment: a national total that looks fine while half the sub-geographies are blank.

entries.name: ILOSTAT
entries.why: Labour statistics for 180-odd countries, sourced from national offices with visible lag.

entries.name: UN World Population Prospects
entries.why: A biennial revision that restates history as well as projections, labelled by revision year.

entries.name: UNdata
entries.why: An aggregator over dozens of UN agencies, so every series here has a primary elsewhere.

entries.name: UNDP Human Development Reports
entries.why: A composite index whose inputs are all elsewhere in the registry, good for lineage demos.

entries.name: UNESCO Institute for Statistics
entries.why: Education indicators with large gaps by country and year, which segments completeness.

entries.name: UNHCR Refugee Data Finder
entries.why: Population-of-concern figures revised mid-year as situations are reassessed.

entries.name: IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix
entries.why: Round-based field assessments, so the freshness question is which round, not which day.

entries.name: IPUMS International
entries.reason: Access requires a per-researcher agreement that forbids redistributing extracts. A router cannot honour a per-user agreement on the caller's behalf, so this stays out of the catalog unless the caller brings their own account under Phase 2 pass-through.
entries.why: The cleanest harmonised census microdata anywhere, and the clearest licence wall.

entries.name: US Census Population Estimates Program
entries.why: Annual estimates that are revised for every year back to the last census, on a vintage.

entries.name: Current Population Survey
entries.why: The survey behind the headline unemployment rate, which lets BLS be checked against source.

entries.name: Business Dynamics Statistics
entries.why: Firm entry and exit with disclosure-suppressed cells, a completeness case with a reason.

entries.name: County Business Patterns
entries.why: Employment by county and industry, where noise infusion changes values between vintages.

entries.name: USAJOBS
entries.why: Live postings that appear and vanish, so the archive is the only record of what existed.

entries.name: O*NET Web Services
entries.why: The occupation taxonomy other job data joins on, versioned explicitly by release.

entries.name: NCES IPEDS
entries.why: Institution-level reporting with provisional and revised releases of the same year.

entries.name: College Scorecard
entries.why: A derivative of IPEDS and tax records, which makes the lag between them measurable.

entries.name: DOL OFLC Performance Data
entries.why: Quarterly visa application disclosures, posted late often enough to be worth measuring.

entries.name: Social Security Administration Open Data
entries.why: Name frequencies and benefit statistics, annual and stable, a good schema-stability baseline.

entries.name: WorldPop
entries.why: Modelled gridded population, so the method version matters more than the timestamp.

entries.name: Human Mortality Database
entries.why: Life tables built from national registers, with a per-country update log to check lag against.

groups.description: Court records, legislation, patents, and trademarks. Two things make this group distinctive. Documents are append-only by nature, which suits an archive, and several of the richest sources charge per page or per seat, which puts the licence question first rather than last. Nothing here is routable until the terms are read, and several entries exist to record a no.

entries.name: CourtListener and RECAP
entries.why: Federal dockets mirrored from PACER, with an explicit date_modified per docket entry.

entries.name: PACER
entries.reason: PACER charges per page retrieved. A router that fetches on a caller's behalf would be spending the customer's money per request, which needs pass-through credentials, a cost ceiling in the envelope, and terms review. None of that exists before Phase 2.
entries.why: The primary that CourtListener is derivative of, which is why the lineage matters.

entries.name: GovInfo
entries.why: Bills, opinions, and the CFR with authenticated PDFs, so hashes can be checked upstream.

entries.name: Caselaw Access Project
entries.why: Digitised state reporters back to 1658, a static corpus that tests as_of replay cheaply.

entries.name: EUR-Lex
entries.why: EU law in 24 languages, where completeness by language is a real segment gap.

entries.name: legislation.gov.uk
entries.why: Point-in-time versions of every statute, which is exactly the as_of model we sell.

entries.name: UK Parliament APIs
entries.why: Bill stages and divisions in near real time, a fast clock in a slow domain.

entries.name: UN Treaty Collection
entries.why: Ratification status by state, corrected quietly, which is a correction-latency case.

entries.name: PatentsView
entries.why: Disambiguated inventors and assignees, a derivative whose method version changes results.

entries.name: USPTO Open Data Portal
entries.why: The primary grants and applications feed that PatentsView derives from.

entries.name: USPTO TSDR
entries.why: Trademark status transitions with dated events, which makes status lag measurable.

entries.name: EPO Open Patent Services
entries.why: European family data, with a free quota and a hard cap that belongs in the envelope.

entries.name: WIPO PATENTSCOPE
entries.why: PCT applications and national collections in one place, licence terms unread so far.

entries.name: GLEIF Legal Entity Identifier
entries.why: The identifier that joins company records across every other source in this registry.

entries.name: OpenCorporates
entries.why: Company registry aggregation under share-alike terms, which forces the share_alike flag in license_chain to be exercised for real rather than hypothetically.

entries.name: ICIJ Offshore Leaks Database
entries.why: A static graph with strict attribution conditions, good for testing attribution strings.

entries.name: CFPB Consumer Complaint Database
entries.why: Daily appends with narratives, which is a live test of the untrusted_text quarantine.

entries.name: CanLII
entries.why: Canadian case law, and a likely noncommercial-only entry to exercise use-class routing.

entries.name: Oyez
entries.why: Supreme Court case metadata and argument audio, a small clean corpus for the console.

entries.name: ECHR HUDOC
entries.why: Strasbourg judgments with translations arriving months later, a completeness-by-language case.

groups.description: Encyclopaedic and reference corpora, plus security advisory feeds. The reference sources are where schema drift and revision behaviour are most extreme, which makes them good stress tests. The security feeds are the clearest case of correction latency mattering to somebody: a CVE amended a week late is a week of wrong answers.

entries.name: Wikidata
entries.why: CC0, edited constantly, so it is the most extreme revision behaviour we could score.

entries.name: Wikipedia API
entries.why: Share-alike text and an enormous untrusted-text surface. Both worth handling properly.

entries.name: DBpedia
entries.why: Structured derivative of Wikipedia, so the lag is measurable against the primary.

entries.name: Open Library
entries.why: Bibliographic records, community edited, with steady completeness improvement.

entries.name: Internet Archive
entries.why: Wayback captures are a second opinion on what a source said at a past time.

entries.name: MusicBrainz
entries.why: Open music metadata with a strict rate limit and a clear attribution policy.

entries.name: Open Food Facts
entries.why: Crowd-sourced product data where completeness varies enormously by country segment.

entries.name: Open Brewery DB
entries.why: Small, stable, and free. A useful low-stakes fixture for adapter tests.

entries.name: Nager.Date public holidays
entries.why: Holiday calendars, which every release-schedule calculation eventually needs.

entries.name: REST Countries
entries.why: Country reference data, the join key for international sources.

entries.name: IANA root zone and TLD registry
entries.why: Rarely changes, so it is an excellent schema-stability control case.

entries.name: Public Suffix List
entries.why: Underpins any domain-level grouping we do, and changes in small reviewable diffs.

entries.name: Unicode CLDR
entries.why: Locale data on a fixed twice-yearly release schedule.

entries.name: NVD CVE API
entries.why: Severity scores are revised after publication, and lateness has a real security cost.

entries.name: CVE Program records
entries.why: The primary that NVD enriches, so the pair proves lineage in a domain people care about.

entries.name: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities
entries.why: Small, authoritative, appended on a schedule. A clean freshness case.

entries.name: GitHub Advisory Database
entries.why: Package-level advisories, another derivative of CVE with its own curation lag.

entries.name: OSV.dev
entries.why: Open vulnerability format aggregating several databases, so disagreement is visible.

entries.name: EPSS exploit prediction scores
entries.why: Daily rescored predictions, which is accuracy with a settleable outcome later.

entries.name: Have I Been Pwned
entries.why: Breach metadata only. Never route to the account-lookup path from a shared key.

groups.description: Biomedical, scholarly, environmental, and public health feeds. This group carries the regulatory wedge (openFDA and friends) and the sources with the most interesting revision and completeness behaviour, because science corrects itself in public and on a schedule.

entries.name: openFDA
entries.why: MAUDE, 510(k), and recalls. The regulatory wedge, with duplicate reports to dedupe.

entries.name: ClinicalTrials.gov
entries.why: Trial records are amended continuously, with an explicit last-update timestamp.

entries.name: PubMed E-utilities
entries.why: Citation metadata at scale, with retractions as a correction-latency signal.

entries.name: PubMed Central Open Access subset
entries.why: Full text under per-article licences, which makes licence chaining concrete.

entries.name: Semantic Scholar
entries.why: Derivative of Crossref and others, so it is a second lineage test outside weather.

entries.name: OpenAlex
entries.why: Open scholarly graph, explicitly CC0, and a clean primary for citation lineage.

entries.name: Crossref
entries.why: DOI registration is the primary that OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar both derive from.

entries.name: arXiv API
entries.why: Versioned preprints, where revision is a first-class concept in the source itself.

entries.name: GBIF Global Biodiversity Information Facility
entries.why: Species occurrence records with per-dataset licences, so licence chaining is forced.

entries.name: NIH RePORTER
entries.why: Grant funding records, a completeness case broken out by institute.

entries.name: CDC Open Data
entries.why: Weekly series that backfill for weeks, the strongest revision-over-time example.

entries.name: CDC WONDER
entries.why: Mortality and natality with suppression rules that make completeness explicit.

entries.name: WHO Global Health Observatory
entries.why: International health indicators, a derivative of national statistical agencies.

entries.name: NPPES NPI Registry
entries.why: Provider identity, the join key for most US healthcare data work.

entries.name: RxNorm
entries.why: Drug terminology, the normalisation layer under any medication query.

entries.name: DailyMed
entries.why: Structured product labelling, updated when manufacturers file changes.

entries.name: USGS Water Services
entries.why: Values are flagged provisional then approved, so revisions are labelled by the source.

entries.name: AirNow
entries.why: Official US air quality, the primary that OpenAQ republishes.

entries.name: OpenAQ
entries.why: Aggregator of AirNow and others, a lineage pair with no licence complication.

entries.name: EPA ECHO
entries.why: Enforcement and compliance history, part of the regulatory wedge.

groups.description: Package registries and the services that index them. This group is the closest thing the registry has to a control group: releases are immutable once published, timestamps are exact, and cadence is high, so a freshness number here is unusually clean. It is also where lineage is obvious, since every aggregator names the registries it mirrors and lags them by hours.

entries.name: npm Registry
entries.why: A changes feed with sequence numbers, which gives an exact ordering to measure lag against.

entries.name: PyPI JSON API
entries.why: Per-project metadata with per-file hashes, so the content hash can be checked upstream.

entries.name: crates.io
entries.why: Publishes both an API and a nightly database dump, so live and cached can be compared.

entries.name: RubyGems
entries.why: Another registry with a versions index, cheap to poll and easy to diff.

entries.name: Packagist
entries.why: PHP ecosystem coverage, with a metadata mirror that lags the primary measurably.

entries.name: Maven Central
entries.why: Coordinates and checksums for the JVM, where artifacts are immutable by policy.

entries.name: NuGet
entries.why: A catalog resource designed for incremental consumption, which suits snapshotting.

entries.name: Go Module Proxy and Index
entries.why: The checksum database is a transparency log already, which is worth studying for Phase 2.

entries.name: Hex.pm
entries.why: Small enough to snapshot whole, which makes completeness trivially verifiable.

entries.name: CRAN via METACRAN
entries.why: CRAN archives old versions on a schedule, so availability changes without the data changing.

entries.name: conda-forge
entries.why: Channel index files republished on every build, a high-churn schema-stability case.

entries.name: Docker Hub Registry
entries.why: Tags are mutable while digests are not, which is the clearest example of why we hash.

entries.name: Homebrew Formulae API
entries.why: A single JSON file for the whole catalog, plus install analytics that revise daily.

entries.name: Debian Package Sources
entries.why: Per-suite indexes where the same package differs by suite, a completeness segment case.

entries.name: Arch Linux Package API
entries.why: A rolling release, so version churn is continuous rather than stepped.

entries.name: Repology
entries.why: Compares the same package across 300 distributions, which is our compare tool already built by somebody else, and therefore the obvious benchmark for ours.

entries.name: Libraries.io
entries.why: A derivative index across registries whose lag behind each primary is easy to measure.

entries.name: Ecosyste.ms
entries.why: Open infrastructure covering the same ground as Libraries.io, so the two can be compared.

entries.name: Open Source Insights (deps.dev)
entries.why: Dependency graphs with advisory joins, which links this group to the security feeds.

entries.name: endoflife.date
entries.why: Community-maintained support dates that change without notice, a correction-latency case.

groups.description: Orbital elements, planetary ephemerides, and astronomical archives. Astronomy solved provenance before anyone called it that: catalogs carry bibcodes, data releases are numbered, and alerts carry the instrument and the exposure that produced them. That makes this group less a source of customers than a source of prior art, plus a few feeds that decay fast enough to make freshness lag obvious. Orbital elements are stale within days, and everyone knows it.

entries.name: CelesTrak
entries.why: Two-line element sets whose accuracy decays measurably with age, which makes freshness lag a physical quantity rather than a convention.

entries.name: Space-Track.org
entries.why: The primary CelesTrak derives from, behind a per-account agreement that limits redistribution, so it can only ever be a pass-through source.

entries.name: JPL Horizons
entries.why: Ephemerides computed on request against a named kernel version, which is reproducibility with the method version already in the response.

entries.name: JPL CNEOS Close Approach Data
entries.why: Predictions that are revised as new observations arrive, with the solution date attached.

entries.name: Minor Planet Center
entries.why: Designations that change as objects are linked and merged, which is renaming as revision.

entries.name: NASA Exoplanet Archive
entries.why: Every parameter carries its reference, so per-row lineage exists without inference.

entries.name: Mikulski Archive for Space Telescopes
entries.why: Observations are reprocessed with new calibrations, so the same exposure changes values.

entries.name: ESA Gaia Archive
entries.why: Numbered data releases that supersede without deleting, which is our snapshot model.

entries.name: SIMBAD
entries.why: An object database curated from the literature, updated daily, with edit dates exposed.

entries.name: VizieR
entries.why: Thousands of published catalogs behind one interface, each with its own citation.

entries.name: NASA/IPAC Extragalactic Database
entries.why: Cross-identifications between catalogs, which is entity resolution with a paper trail.

entries.name: NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive
entries.why: Mission archives with explicit release versions, another reprocessing case.

entries.name: AAVSO Variable Star Index
entries.why: Amateur observations moderated before publication, a correction-latency case with humans.

entries.name: General Coordinates Network
entries.why: Transient alerts in seconds, then refined for hours, which is the fastest revise-in-public cycle in the registry and the sharpest correction-latency test available.

entries.name: Transient Name Server
entries.why: The naming authority that GCN reports resolve to, so the two can be checked against each other.

entries.name: ALeRCE Alert Broker
entries.why: A broker over survey alerts whose classifications change as more data arrives.

entries.name: NOIRLab Astro Data Archive
entries.why: Raw and reduced frames side by side, with proprietary periods that expire on a date.

entries.name: SDSS SkyServer
entries.why: Every data release stays queryable forever, which is as_of replay already implemented.

entries.name: ESA Space Weather Service Network
entries.why: A European read on the same solar events as NOAA SWPC, which makes disagreement visible.

entries.name: USGS Astrogeology Planetary Data
entries.why: Planetary basemaps versioned by product, slow enough to be a schema-stability baseline.

groups.description: MCP servers for payments, commerce, CRM, support, marketing, and communications. Several of these can move money or send messages on a customer's behalf. Promotion of any entry with a write path requires the confirmation rules in the runbook to be written first; Trooth routes reads by default and never exposes a write tool without an explicit ADR.

entries.name: Stripe
entries.why: We will already run Stripe for billing, so it is the cheapest hosted server to test.

entries.name: PayPal
entries.why: Payments coverage.

entries.name: Square
entries.why: Point-of-sale and small business payments.

entries.name: Shopify
entries.why: Catalog, inventory, and order data, where staleness has a direct cost.

entries.name: BigCommerce
entries.why: Commerce coverage.

entries.name: Salesforce
entries.why: The CRM enterprises run, and the most valuable pass-through target we could support.

entries.name: HubSpot
entries.why: CRM coverage for smaller teams, with a usable free tier for testing.

entries.name: Zendesk
entries.why: Support tickets, which are untrusted text with a clear event time.

entries.name: Intercom
entries.why: Support and messaging coverage.

entries.name: Freshdesk
entries.why: Support coverage.

entries.name: Pipedrive
entries.why: CRM coverage.

entries.name: Mailchimp
entries.why: Campaign data, with a send path that must stay behind confirmation.

entries.name: Klaviyo
entries.why: Commerce marketing coverage.

entries.name: Twilio
entries.why: Messaging and voice, and a metered upstream whose cost belongs in the envelope quota.

entries.name: SendGrid
entries.why: Transactional mail coverage.

entries.name: Resend
entries.why: Developer-first mail, likely what we use for alerts.

entries.name: Plaid
entries.why: Bank data strictly under the customer's own credentials, never redistributed.

entries.name: Alpaca
entries.why: Market data and brokerage; read-only routing, no order path, ever.

entries.name: QuickBooks
entries.why: Accounting data for small business agents.

entries.name: Xero
entries.why: Accounting coverage outside the United States.

groups.description: MCP servers for analytics warehouses, vector and graph stores, and web search or crawl. Search and crawl servers carry the largest untrusted-text surface in the catalog, so every promotion here needs the H5 quarantine path exercised before it merges.

entries.name: DuckDB
entries.why: Reads our Parquet archive directly, so it is the reference client for as-of replay.

entries.name: ClickHouse
entries.why: Column store with a free tier, a plausible home for the snapshot archive at scale.

entries.name: Snowflake
entries.why: Enterprise warehouse, the most requested pass-through target in sales conversations.

entries.name: Databricks
entries.why: Lakehouse coverage.

entries.name: BigQuery
entries.why: Hosts many free public datasets, some of which are catalog candidates in their own right.

entries.name: Elasticsearch
entries.why: Self-hosted search coverage.

entries.name: Algolia
entries.why: Hosted search coverage.

entries.name: Meilisearch
entries.why: Open-source search, cheap to self-host alongside the console.

entries.name: Typesense
entries.why: Open-source search alternative.

entries.name: Pinecone
entries.why: The most common hosted vector store in agent stacks.

entries.name: Qdrant
entries.why: Open-source vector store with a documented server.

entries.name: Weaviate
entries.why: Vector store coverage.

entries.name: Chroma
entries.why: Local vector store, useful in offline evals.

entries.name: Neo4j
entries.why: Graph queries, and the obvious store for the lineage graph itself.

entries.name: Exa
entries.why: Neural web search, with results that are entirely untrusted text.

entries.name: Tavily
entries.why: Agent-oriented search, widely used and a good injection-surface test case.

entries.name: Perplexity
entries.why: Answer engine, where provenance is asserted but not verifiable.

entries.name: Brave Search
entries.why: Independent web index with a free tier.

entries.name: Firecrawl
entries.why: Page-to-markdown crawling, the highest-risk untrusted-text path we would route to.

entries.name: Apify
entries.why: Scraper marketplace, and a preview of the Phase 3 provider model.

groups.description: MCP servers covering source control, issue tracking, code quality, CI, and containers. Every entry is a candidate under ADR-0010 until a promotion PR confirms its terms from the vendor's own documentation. license_status unverified means nobody has read the terms yet.

entries.name: GitHub
entries.why: Repository, issue, and pull request access is the most requested agent tool surface.

entries.name: GitLab
entries.why: Second source-control surface, needed before any enterprise conversation.

entries.name: Bitbucket
entries.why: Completes source control coverage for Atlassian shops.

entries.name: Git (local repository)
entries.why: Local-only server with no network calls, useful as a zero-risk routing test case.

entries.name: Filesystem
entries.why: The canonical reference server, and the clearest example of a tool with no provenance.

entries.name: Linear
entries.why: Issue tracking is where agent workflows start, and Linear ships a hosted server.

entries.name: Jira
entries.why: The issue tracker most enterprises actually run.

entries.name: Confluence
entries.why: Internal documentation retrieval, the most common private RAG target.

entries.name: SonarQube
entries.why: Code quality metrics as a routed source, with a self-hosted option.

entries.name: Snyk
entries.why: Vulnerability data with a revision pattern worth scoring; advisories get amended.

entries.name: Semgrep
entries.why: Static analysis with an open rules corpus.

entries.name: CircleCI
entries.why: Build status as a feed, with exact event timestamps for freshness scoring.

entries.name: Jenkins
entries.why: Self-hosted CI, the common case in regulated environments.

entries.name: Buildkite
entries.why: CI coverage for teams that run their own agents.

entries.name: Docker
entries.why: Container inspection and image metadata, a common agent operations task.

entries.name: Kubernetes
entries.why: Cluster state is the clearest pass-through credential case in the catalog.

entries.name: Terraform
entries.why: Registry metadata and plan inspection for infrastructure agents.

entries.name: Pulumi
entries.why: Second infrastructure-as-code surface.

entries.name: E2B
entries.why: Sandboxed execution, useful for evaluating tools before routing to them.

entries.name: Playwright
entries.why: Browser automation, and the largest untrusted-text surface of any common server.

groups.description: MCP servers for cloud platforms, managed databases, hosting, and observability. Most of these are reached with the customer's own credentials, so they are the natural first users of pass-through auth (ADR-0008) rather than anything Trooth redistributes.

entries.name: Amazon Web Services
entries.why: The largest cloud surface, and pass-through credentials are the only way to reach it.

entries.name: Microsoft Azure
entries.why: Second cloud, required for enterprise parity.

entries.name: Google Cloud
entries.why: Third cloud, and the path to BigQuery as a routed source.

entries.name: Cloudflare
entries.why: We run on Cloudflare, so this is the one we can test end to end at zero cost.

entries.name: Vercel
entries.why: Deployment state for front-end agents.

entries.name: Netlify
entries.why: Alternative hosting surface.

entries.name: Fly.io
entries.why: Machine and region state for latency-sensitive deployments.

entries.name: Railway
entries.why: Hosting coverage for smaller teams.

entries.name: Render
entries.why: Hosting coverage.

entries.name: DigitalOcean
entries.why: Hosting coverage, and a cheap place to run a self-hosted console.

entries.name: Supabase
entries.why: Managed Postgres with a documented server, common in agent side projects.

entries.name: Neon
entries.why: Serverless Postgres with branching, a good demonstration of as-of replay.

entries.name: PlanetScale
entries.why: Managed MySQL coverage.

entries.name: MongoDB
entries.why: Document database coverage, and schema stability scoring where there is no schema.

entries.name: Redis
entries.why: Cache inspection, relevant to the served_from field in the envelope.

entries.name: PostgreSQL
entries.why: The reference database server, and the most common customer-owned source.

entries.name: Grafana
entries.why: Both a routed source and the free dashboard tool we document in ADR-0011.

entries.name: Prometheus
entries.why: Time series with exact scrape timestamps, so freshness lag is unambiguous.

entries.name: Datadog
entries.why: Commercial observability coverage.

entries.name: Sentry
entries.why: Error events with a clear event time, and a hosted server to test against.

groups.description: MCP servers for messaging, mail, calendars, documents, files, design, and task tracking. Almost all of these reach private customer data, so they are pass-through by default and none of their content is ever cached by Trooth beyond the customer's own private cache.

entries.name: Notion
entries.why: Hosted server, broad adoption, and a clean OAuth flow to model pass-through on.

entries.name: Slack
entries.why: Where teams already are, and a large untrusted-text surface worth quarantining well.

entries.name: Discord
entries.why: Community messaging coverage.

entries.name: Gmail
entries.why: Mail access, the most sensitive pass-through case and the one to get right first.

entries.name: Google Calendar
entries.why: Scheduling data with exact event timestamps.

entries.name: Google Drive
entries.why: Document retrieval, the most common private RAG source.

entries.name: Microsoft 365
entries.why: Graph covers mail, files, calendar, and Teams behind one enterprise credential.

entries.name: Outlook
entries.why: Mail coverage for Microsoft shops, likely folded into the Graph entry.

entries.name: Box
entries.why: Regulated-industry file storage.

entries.name: Dropbox
entries.why: File storage coverage.

entries.name: Asana
entries.why: Work tracking outside engineering teams.

entries.name: monday.com
entries.why: Work management coverage.

entries.name: ClickUp
entries.why: Work management coverage.

entries.name: Trello
entries.why: Lightweight task boards.

entries.name: Todoist
entries.why: Personal task management, a common first agent integration.

entries.name: Obsidian
entries.why: Local notes, entirely offline, with no redistribution question at all.

entries.name: Airtable
entries.why: Structured customer data with a real schema, useful for schema stability scoring.

entries.name: Figma
entries.why: Design context for agents that write front-end code.

entries.name: Canva
entries.why: Design asset coverage.

entries.name: Zoom
entries.why: Meeting transcripts, which are untrusted text with a precise event time.
